text: The paper translates Ostrom's commons principles into validation-pool boundaries, proportional allocation, protocol governance, output verification, graduated sanctions, appeals, community ownership, and nested pools.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Reinforcement Learning from Reputation Feedback (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7456999
abstract: Within the RLRF mechanism speciﬁcally, Ostrom’s design principles translate as follows. Clearly deﬁned boundaries correspond to non-transferable domain-speciﬁc reputation (Section III.B). Proportionality corresponds to reputation-weighted allocation of validation opportunity (equation 1). Collective-choice arrangements correspond to on- chain protocol governance. Effective monitoring corresponds to cryptographic veriﬁcation of outputs against stated objective functions. Graduated sanctions correspond to the MWU asymmetry . Conﬂict-resolution mechanisms correspond to dispute protocols with appeal pathways. Recognition of self-governance corresponds to community ownership of the validation protocol. Nested enterprises correspond to layered validation pools composing into federated networks through veri ﬁed cross- network reputation.
